events.what: Self-published Zenodo cluster by 'Giovanni Esposito' claims nonexistence of odd distinct covering systems
events.credibility_reason: Several F5 signals together: a landmark Erdős problem, no expert uptake in eight months, the tracker (erdosproblems.com) still lists it as open and does not cite it, no findable author affiliation, and invented jargon ('arithmetic renormalization', 'obstruction energy') unconnected to known techniques.

events.what: Forum user jinooklee with Aristotle claims a Lean-backed nonexistence proof extending BBMST; Sothanaphan finds a false axiom, submitter concedes
events.credibility_reason: Axiom 'bbmst_sf_lt_one' shown false (Sothanaphan, May 6); submitter acknowledged the axiom was 'provably false' and the claim was withdrawn.
events.ai_basis: submitted ... together with the AI theorem-proving system Aristotle (Harmonic)

events.what: Mian & Siddique give a Lean 4 kernel-checked formalization of the known bound that any odd covering has lcm > 10000
events.ai_basis: 'Development was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic)' — formalisation of a known result; formalising is none

judgement.doubts: The record's 'progress' came from treating a withdrawn claim as an instructive incident; under §4 a knocked-down claim cannot set status. The Mian–Siddique paper formalises an already-known bound (the record calls it known/folklore), so it moves nothing. Event object left as is for evidence; it describes the knocked-down Aristotle claim, not a status-bearing event.

corrections.why: F6: the Aristotle claim was withdrawn after the submitter conceded the axiom was 'provably false'; F5: the Esposito cluster is not credible; the Mian–Siddique paper is a formalisation of a 'known/folklore' bound (scope none). No event survives and nothing was resolved pre-snapshot.
F6/F8: ai_role describes the event the status rests on; no event survives, so none. The Aristotle involvement remains documented in ai.basis_quote as evidence.
